connectors.name: OBD-II / EOBD 16-pin, Type A (SAE J1962 / ISO 15031-3)
connectors.applies_to: Petrol cars sold in the US from 1996 and the EU from 2001, diesels in the EU from 2004; most light vans
connectors.description: Trapezoid 16-pin socket in two rows of 8, usually within reach of the driver under the dashboard.
connectors.adapter: Any ELM327-compatible OBD-II adapter (USB, Bluetooth or Wi-Fi). K-line vehicles also work with a raw K-line cable (KKL / FTDI).
connectors.support_note: Generic OBD-II scan, live data and clearing are implemented and simulator-tested, not yet verified on real vehicles.
warnings: Pins 1, 3, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 13 belong to the manufacturer. Some carry programming voltage (e.g. Ford pin 13): never connect anything to them without a model-specific definition.

sources.note: SAE J1962 pin assignment with cited standards
CARB 13 CCR 1962.5: electric cars from MY2026 must have a J1962 Type A connector

notes: Examples of manufacturer pins (Wikipedia, medium confidence): GM single-wire CAN on 1, Ford/Chrysler buses on 3 and 11, a second K-line on 8 on many BMWs.
Electric cars: California requires a J1962 Type A connector on electric cars from model year 2026 (40%) and 2027 (100%). Older electric cars often have no standard diagnostics.

pinout.signal: Ethernet pair A + (option 1; sources disagree on RX/TX direction)

connectors.adapter: An Ethernet (ENET/DoIP) cable; ELM327 adapters cannot do Ethernet.
connectors.support_note: DoIP is planned for a later phase.
warnings: The direction of the pairs and the activation resistance must be confirmed from ISO 13400 before any implementation.

sources.note: SAE J1962 pin assignment with cited standards

notes: Option 2 uses pins 1 and 9 instead of 3 and 11 for the first pair (python-doipclient).

how_to_read: Find the procedure for your exact model and year in its service manual before touching the connector.
Ignition off. Bridge only the terminals the manual names, with the correct jumper or service tool.
Switch the ignition on (engine off) and watch the warning light; use the reader below to count long and short flashes.

connectors.name: Euro 5 motorcycle 6-pin (ISO 19689)

sources.note: lists CRF1100L 2020–2023 among bikes with the Euro 5 6-pin

notes: Pin assignment from a data-logger maker (AiM), not from the ISO text; pin 1 is not listed.
Enduro (L3e-AxE), trial (L3e-AxT), mopeds and some light vehicles are exempt from stage II.
The regulation also allows the 16-pin ISO 15031-3 connector instead.

connectors.name: Honda motorcycle 4-pin red DLC
connectors.applies_to: Fuel-injected (PGM-FI) Honda bikes from about 2003, e.g. CBR600RR 2003+, CTX700, CRF250L; CRF1000L Africa Twin 2016–2019 has a DLC under the seat (pin count not confirmed for that model)
connectors.description: Red 4-pin connector (often with a dummy plug), usually under the seat.
protocols: Blink codes via the SCS service connector
connectors.adapter: For data: a raw K-line cable (FTDI-type USB serial with a K-line transceiver) wired to the 4-pin DLC. For blink codes: Honda's SCS service connector 070PZ-ZY30100 or equivalent jumper.
connectors.support_note: Blink codes: OpenDiag's blink-code reader helps you count the flashes and looks them up in a table you copy from your service manual. OpenDiag does not ship the code meanings. Experimental read-only K-line mode (expert mode, raw K-line cable): wake-up and raw table reads, not yet tested on a real bike; sources disagree on the wake-up message. Reading fault codes over the K-line is not implemented.
how_to_read: Ignition off. Remove the dummy plug from the red DLC.
Connect the SCS service connector (Honda 070PZ-ZY30100) to the DLC. The terminals to short differ per model: check the manual.
Switch the ignition on (engine off, kill switch to RUN). The fuel-injection warning light (MIL) blinks the codes.
Long blink (about 1.3 s) = 10, short blink (about 0.3 s) = 1; codes come smallest first. Use the reader below.
Ignition off, remove the SCS connector and refit the dummy plug.
warnings: Bridging the wrong terminals can damage the engine control unit. If you are not sure which terminals to use, do not guess.
On the CRF1000L, disconnecting the battery does not clear stored codes (manual excerpt quoted on a forum).
notes: The pinout comes from one open-source project; a second agrees on the functions but gives no numbers.
A generic ELM327 does not work: Honda does not use the ISO wake-up and uses a different checksum.
